Changelog

Release history for taxodist, from version 0.1.0 through the coordinated 0.9.0 implementations.

taxodist 0.1.0 — Initial release

  • Introduced taxonomic distance calculations using lineage data from The Taxonomicon.
  • Added session-level lineage caching to reduce repeated network requests.
  • Initial functions: taxo_distance(), mrca(), distance_matrix(), closest_relative(), compare_lineages(), shared_clades(), is_member(), filter_clade(), lineage_depth(), check_coverage(), and clear_cache().

taxodist 0.2.0

New functions

  • Added taxo_cluster() for hierarchical clustering of taxonomic distances.
  • Added taxo_ordinate() for principal coordinates analysis (PCoA).
  • Added save_cache() and load_cache() for persistence across sessions.
  • Added taxo_path(), which represents the node-by-node route from taxon A through the MRCA to taxon B.

Documentation and integration

  • Added statistical examples using vegan for taxonomic distinctness, Mantel tests, and PERMANOVA.
  • Documented conversion of taxo_cluster() results to the phylo storage class with ape::as.phylo().

Corrections

  • Prevented unnamed crown markers from being interpreted as common ancestry across unrelated lineages.
  • Expanded cleaning of rank prefixes such as cohort, magnorder, grandorder, parvorder, and legion.

taxodist 0.3.0

Name resolution and network handling

  • Added taxo_search() for inspecting Taxonomicon search results and numeric identifiers.
  • Added direct support for numeric Taxonomicon IDs in get_lineage() and downstream distance functions.
  • Added request timeouts and clearer handling of network failures and non-successful HTTP responses.
  • Added warnings for multiple valid biological entries, making homonym ambiguity explicit.

Lineage parsing

  • Expanded removal of rank labels and navigation artifacts.
  • Collapsed duplicated lineage nodes while preserving their original order.
  • Improved taxonomic redirect handling and removal of interface noise.
  • Restricted cleaned lineages to nodes beginning at Biota when available.
  • Added validation for non-numeric inputs to get_lineage_by_id().
  • Corrected species-level lineages, quoted author names, and genus retention.

taxodist 0.4.0

New functions

  • Added cache_info() to report cached lineages, identifiers, and memory use.
  • Added focal_distances() to compare one focal taxon with every member of a community while reporting distance, MRCA, and MRCA depth.

Lineage parsing

  • Corrected handling of Subphylum and Infraphylum prefixes.
  • Improved removal of extinction markers, auct. annotations, author strings, ampersands, hyphenated names, and incomplete trailing citations.

taxodist 0.5.0

Reference data

  • Added taxobase, an offline reference object containing taxa, coverage information, lineages, search examples, pairwise results, and precomputed distance matrices.

Corrections

  • Prevented biological names containing the substring planet, such as Periplaneta, from being classified as astronomical entries.
  • Corrected lineage truncation when a genus page does not link directly back to the genus itself.
  • Added Epifamily to the rank-token filter.
  • Corrected parsing around superscript type markers and target names appearing in page-navigation text.

taxodist 0.6.0

Distance definition

  • Zero distance is now reserved for identical complete lineages.
  • Distinct ancestor–descendant nodes receive \(1 / \operatorname{depth}(\operatorname{MRCA})\) rather than zero.
  • The measure is now described consistently as a taxonomic hierarchy distance, not a phylogenetic distance.
  • Within each connected hierarchy, the resulting distance is an ultrametric.
Behavioral change

Analyses that relied on version 0.5.0 or earlier should be recomputed when ancestor–descendant pairs are present. Use is_member() for clade containment and taxo_path() to inspect the route between hierarchy nodes.

Data and documentation

  • Standardized taxobase as a documented list with provenance metadata and offline matrices used by reproducible examples.
  • Aligned the R, Python, and Julia reference data, taxon ordering, distance definition, and principal API behavior.
  • Added explicit methodological documentation, limitations, and separate citations for the software and The Taxonomicon.
  • Revised statistical examples to distinguish taxonomic dendrograms from inferred phylogenetic trees.
  • Added the Julia implementation and registered distribution, with the same distance definition, principal API, labeled matrices, cache persistence, analysis helpers, and packaged taxobase reference data.

Robustness

  • MRCA detection now uses only the continuous common prefix of the two ordered lineages.
  • is_member() now uses exact, case-insensitive matching.
  • taxo_path() now handles identical nodes, ancestor–descendant pairs, full lineage depths, path direction, and lineages without a common ancestor.
  • Empty and single-taxon inputs are handled consistently across matrix, nearest-relative, focal-distance, clustering, ordination, and heatmap functions.
  • Clustering, ordination, and heatmap helpers detect missing and infinite distances before downstream analysis.
  • taxo_ordinate() validates and, when necessary, reduces the requested number of dimensions.
  • load_cache() validates names and value types before modifying the active cache.

Cross-language compatibility note

The R, Python, and Julia implementations follow the same distance semantics. Their native containers differ: R uses dist, S3 objects, and .rds cache files; Python uses labeled pandas objects, dictionaries, and .pkl cache files; Julia uses TaxonomicDistanceMatrix, named tuples, DataFrame objects, and .json cache files.

taxodist 0.7.0

Performance

  • R now fills the compact lower-triangular dist representation directly instead of allocating a full square intermediate matrix.
  • Python now reuses a persistent HTTP session across Taxonomicon requests, enabling connection pooling without changing public behavior.
  • All three implementations use streamlined numeric pairwise paths for matrix construction and reuse final name-resolved lineages during warm calls.

Compatibility and validation

  • Preserved the public API and continuous-prefix MRCA distance semantics.
  • Revalidated reference matrices, resolved identifiers, lineage outputs, and optimized matrix paths across R, Python, and Julia.
  • Julia now reads intermediate hierarchy nodes rendered as plain text and aligns ambiguous-name matching with the whole-word behavior used by R and Python.
  • Expanded deterministic and regression coverage; each implementation reports complete coverage under its language-specific coverage measure.
  • Improved cache inspection and clearing in the R implementation by addressing the private cache environment explicitly.

taxodist 0.8.0

Auditable name resolution

  • Added taxo_resolve() for batch resolution with explicit resolved, ambiguous, unresolved, and retrieval_error statuses.
  • Preserved all candidate matches, selected identifiers, resolved names, lineage depths, and root-to-tip lineages for every input.
  • Added explicit ambiguity policies: warn and select the first candidate, select silently, or stop and require review.
  • Repeated names are retrieved only once while their original order and repetition remain in the audit table.
  • distance_matrix() accepts resolution objects directly and reuses stored lineages without further network requests.

Offline classifications

  • Added taxo_from_lineages() for curated, frozen, unpublished, or fully offline classifications.
  • Added deterministic custom identifiers and optional user-supplied identifiers.
  • Offline resolutions use the same distance, validation, and bundle APIs as live Taxonomicon resolutions.

Portable analysis bundles

  • Added taxo_bundle() to combine the resolution audit, labeled matrix, metric definition, software metadata, and source provenance.
  • Added write_taxodist_bundle() and read_taxodist_bundle() using a shared JSON schema across R, Python, and Julia.
  • Missing distances use JSON null; disconnected infinities use "Infinity" and "-Infinity".
  • Bundle validation checks required fields, statuses, candidate counts, selected IDs, lineage depths, matrix labels, symmetry, and agreement between stored lineages and distances.

Robustness and compatibility

  • Preserved the continuous-prefix MRCA distance definition and established public workflows.
  • Improved retrieval-error reporting, structured lineage parsing, name-resolution caching, and source provenance.
  • Expanded deterministic regression tests to complete source coverage in all three implementations.

taxodist 0.9.0 Latest

Version 0.9.0 was released simultaneously for R, Python, and Julia. The distance definition and the bundle schema (version 1.0) are unchanged; bundles written by any of the three implementations are read by the other two without differences.

Corrections

  • taxo_resolve() now truncates each selected lineage at the queried taxon exactly as get_lineage() does. Previously it stored the lineage of the retrieved page unchanged; for genera whose page does not list the genus itself (for example Periplaneta), the lineage ended at the family, resolved_name reported the family, and distance_matrix(taxo_resolve(x)) could differ from distance_matrix(x). Bundles built from such resolutions inherited the difference.
  • Cleaned and uncleaned lineages are cached separately. A call with clean = FALSE previously replaced the cleaned entry, so later calls returned nodes above Biota for the rest of the session.
  • Queried names are normalized (surrounding and repeated whitespace) and located in the lineage without regard to letter case. Previously "tyrannosaurus" or "Tyrannosaurus " added a spurious terminal node, increasing lineage depth.
  • taxo_heatmap() passes plotting arguments only to the plotting function (R and Julia previously forwarded them to distance_matrix(); Python rejected cmap and annot). verbose and progress are explicit arguments.
  • cache_info() reports the names of cached taxa together with their identifiers (ids); it previously listed identifiers only.
  • get_lineage_by_id() accepts numeric identifiers and reports an informative error for several identifiers.
  • Python: the User-Agent header and bundle metadata report the installed version, distance_matrix() rejects a single string, and each candidate lineage is retrieved once during disambiguation.

Behavior changes

Changed return values
  • check_coverage() reports an unknown result (NA in R, pd.NA in Python, missing in Julia) when The Taxonomicon could not be reached. Such names were previously reported as absent.
  • save_cache() returns the path of the written file.
  • Using a bundle in distance_matrix() or printing it validates its structure only. The complete recomputation of every stored distance is performed when a bundle is written or read.

New functions and arguments

  • taxo_tree() builds a tree directly from lineages. Internal nodes are the named clades at which the supplied taxa diverge; clades with a single descendant are collapsed. Branch lengths place a clade at depth \(h\) at height \(1/(2h)\), so the tree is ultrametric and its patristic distances equal distance_matrix(). R returns an ape-compatible phylo object; Python and Julia return a TaxodistTree with Newick export.
  • cross_distances(x, y) computes the rectangular matrix between two sets of taxa.
  • compare_bundles(old, new) classifies every input as unchanged, added, removed, or changed in status, identifier, or lineage, and lists the pairwise distances that changed. Bundle files can be passed by path.
  • taxo_resolve() and taxo_bundle() gain within, which restricts candidates to those whose lineage contains a given clade.
  • save_cache() and load_cache() default to a persistent per-user cache file.

Performance and network handling

  • Distance matrices are computed from integer prefix identifiers: each node is mapped to an integer identifying its complete path from the root, so the MRCA depth of two taxa is the number of depths at which the identifiers agree.
  • Requests are retried with exponential backoff after network errors and server errors (5xx); the number of attempts is configurable.

Web application

  • The application uses the 0.9.0 packages, adds a between-groups tab and classification trees, reports names that were not found and the entry chosen for ambiguous names, offers CSV, PNG, Newick, and bundle downloads, and supports links that reopen a query.
  • Its bundled lineage cache was rebuilt; a cache produced by an earlier parser is no longer loaded.
